Eala in blue for the prestigious U.S. Open Several reports disclosed the newest tennis dress – also with Nike – of Eala, particularly for the U.S Open later this month. The color? It was all blue with shades of black and white. Before plunging into U.S Open action, the Southeast Asian Games champion is expected to enter the WTA 1000 Cincinnati Open fray which opens this week in Mason, Ohio. The 5-foot-9 ace is anticipated as well to join the national team next month for the Aichi-Nagoya 20th Asian Games in Japan where she eyes a historic gold for the Philippines.

Marcos to decide on Quiboloy's extradition in 'couple of weeks' — Palace. President Marcos deemed it necessary to think over what action the government would take in response to the United States' request to extradite detained pastor Apollo Quiboloy. Malacañang reiterated that the US request to extradite Quiboloy must undergo a thorough evaluation, stating the President would weigh the options and make a decision in "a couple of weeks." "Opo, nakausap po natin kanina mismo ang Pangulo at sinabi po niya na kailangan po talaga itong pag-aralan mabuti pero in a couple of weeks ay magbibigay po sila ng anunsyo kung ano ang magiging desisyon para dito (Yes, we spoke with the President himself earlier, and he said that this really needs to be carefully studied. However, in a couple of weeks, they will announce what the decision will be on the matter)," Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said on Monday, Aug. 10. According to Castro, extradition is covered by an agreement, specifically the treaty with the US, which includes its provisions. The Philippine government, Castro added, has two options: either Quiboloy remains in the country while the case is heard in the Philippines, or the case here can be temporarily put on hold or suspended, allowing for his extradition and transfer to the United States. The Palace official said she cannot yet say what the President is keen on doing. "In a couple of weeks, saka niya sasabihin kung ano yung pwede niyang stance patungkol dito (In a couple of weeks, he will announce what his position will be on the matter)," Castro said. "So, lahat naman ito ay dapat na dumaan sa proseso dahil may batas naman po tayo. At mag-de-decide po sila, ibibigay niya po kung ano yung dapat na gawin patungkol dito (Everything has to go through the proper process because we have laws in place. They will make a decision, and he will announce what needs to be done regarding the matter)," Castro added. On Aug. 6, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) confirmed it received the US government's request for Quiboloy's extradition and endorsed the matter to the Department of Justice (DOJ). Quiboloy was taken into government custody on Sept. 8, 2024, after he surrendered to authorities inside the 30-hectare KOJC compound in Davao City following a 16-day police operation to serve his arrest warrant.

Manila Water takes full ownership of ₱38-billion Wawa dam project. Razon-led Manila Water Co. is now the sole owner of the Wawa Dam in Rizal after acquiring the remaining stake in WawaJVCo, Inc., allowing the company to boost supply operations across its distribution network. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange on Monday, Aug. 10, Manila Water announced that it secured the remaining minority interest in WawaJVCo to complete its takeover, though it did not disclose the acquisition cost for the remaining stake. This completes a transaction that began last year, when Manila Water entered into a ₱37.8-billion share purchase agreement with Prime Infrastructure, Inc. to reduce its reliance on the Angat Dam. Even as the Wawa Dam expansion promises long-term supply benefits, Manila Water noted that it has kept its non-revenue water (NRW) levels below 15 percent, ensuring steady service across Metro Manila and neighboring provinces despite ongoing rains. According to a company operational report, East Zone NRW stood at 13.51 percent in June 2026, bringing its year-to-date average to 14.22 percent. The performance keeps Manila Water among Asia's top-performing utilities, matching standards set by developed nations. NRW, or unbilled water loss, is typically caused by leaks, pipe bursts, illegal connections, and meter inaccuracies before water reaches consumers. Since assuming control of the concession in 1997, Manila Water has brought its NRW down from a high of 63 percent, noting that every single percentage-point reduction recovers at least 15 million liters of water per day for its customers. To maintain low loss levels, the utility repaired 221 major mainline pipe failures within 24 hours during the first half of the year, including 27 incidents in June alone. Network reliability is especially critical during the rainy season, when shifting ground conditions and heavy rainfall heighten the risk of pipe damage. The company attributed its performance to proactive asset management, round-the-clock monitoring, and prompt leak reporting by local residents. Dittie Galang, Manila Water Corporate Communications Group Head, emphasized the importance of these ongoing efficiency measures. “Keeping water losses at low levels is the result of sustained investments in operational efficiency, proactive asset management, and advanced leak detection technologies. These initiatives help us maximize available water resources, protect critical infrastructure, and ensure dependable service for our customers, especially during challenging weather conditions,” Galang said. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

Women lead Philippines’ booming VA workforce. Women are dominating the Philippines’ virtual assistant (VA) industry, accounting for nearly seven in 10 successful hires as the country remains a major source of remote talent for businesses worldwide. According to the State of the Filipino Virtual Assistant Industry 2026 report by global recruitment agency VA Masters, women accounted for 61.5 percent of 166,350 job applications analyzed and performed better through technical screening, raising their share to 69 percent of successfully placed VAs. The report showed that the candidate pool is also relatively young, with a median applicant age of 28 years. VA Masters said its recruitment process is highly selective, with more than 20,000 people applying to its job postings each month, equivalent to about one application every two minutes. The report also showed that Filipino VAs who secured jobs generally had stronger English proficiency and professional experience than the overall applicant pool. Among all applicants, 62 percent reported fluent or native-level English proficiency, compared with 80 percent among those hired. Meanwhile, 36 percent of applicants had at least three years of specialized professional experience, while 20 percent had more than five years of relevant experience. Among candidates who passed client evaluations and received job offers, 65 percent had at least three years of direct experience in fields such as digital marketing, operations, financial bookkeeping and executive support. “The language proficiency and execution caliber of the Filipino workforce are underappreciated in global commerce,” VA Masters founder and chief executive officer (CEO) Alon Pearl in a statement on Monday, Aug. 10. “We are looking at an exceptionally skilled, English-fluent demographic that delivers high-level execution. This enables growing businesses to expand their operational capacity while reducing labor overhead by up to 80 percent compared to local hiring,” Pearl added. VA Masters said international companies can tap the Philippines’ pool of skilled remote workers across different fields by using strict hiring tests to screen applicants and build support teams. The recruitment agency estimated that the global virtual assistant services market is worth about $6.5 billion in 2026 and could reach nearly $34 billion by 2030. It also estimated that the Philippines accounts for 38 percent of the global VA workforce, making the country the world’s largest source of virtual assistant talent. The growth of remote work opportunities comes as the Philippine labor market showed signs of weakening. The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) last week reported that the unemployment rate rose to 4.9 percent in June from 4.8 percent in May and 3.7 percent a year ago, equivalent to 2.59 million unemployed Filipinos. The expanding VA industry also comes amid increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), which could reshape jobs in related service industries. The World Bank earlier identified the Philippines as a significant participant in the global AI landscape, while flagging the potential impact of the technology on the country’s business process outsourcing (BPO) sector, to which the VA industry is closely related. - Danielle T. Bayani

Slowing economic growth eases pressure on BSP to raise rates. Pressure on the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to raise its benchmark interest rate has eased after economic growth slowed to a post-pandemic low in the second quarter of the year, according to the central bank officials. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the central bank’s stakeholders’ appreciation event on Monday, Aug. 10, BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr. said the monetary authority remains open to further tightening if necessary. The policy-setting Monetary Board will adjust borrowing costs “as much as necessary” to bring inflation back to its three percent target, Remolona said. Headline inflation remained above the four percent target ceiling in July despite easing to a three-month low of 6.2 percent. Meanwhile, core inflation—which strips out volatile food and energy items—has also shown signs of moderation. “Core inflation may have plateaued,” BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja told reporters during the event, highlighting the first deceleration in core inflation in July from a peak of 4.4 percent in June. Abenoja, who oversees the BSP’s Monetary and Economics Sector, noted the downward momentum in price pressures. The three-month low in headline inflation coincided with a second-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) growth outturn of 2.3 percent. According to the BSP chief, policymakers are focusing closely on core inflation rather than the headline figure, as core inflation reflects factors within the central bank's control. “In the headline, there are a lot of supply shocks,” he explained. Further rate hikes could help anchor price movements, but they pose a headwind for growth by dampening private borrowing and consumption. This leaves the BSP balancing its primary price stability mandate with output growth. Remolona affirmed that pressure to hike rates at the upcoming Aug. 27 policy meeting has receded following weaker-than-expected second-quarter GDP performance. Following the August session, the Monetary Board is scheduled to meet next on Oct. 22 and Dec. 17. Abenoja added that the central bank had anticipated soft growth in the first half of the year, expecting firmer signs of recovery to take hold in the second half. The economy continues to feel the effects of dampened confidence stemming from high-profile flood control corruption scandals that unraveled in late 2025. Despite its firm commitment to price stability, Remolona emphasized that the BSP is not ignoring economic growth. “Growth is implied by the inflation mandate. If you can maintain price stability, that tends to sustain growth,” Remolona said. “But in the short run, sometimes there are problems with growth, and we take that into account. We don’t ignore them.” Dutch financial institution ING projects that the BSP may maintain a hawkish stance across upcoming meetings, with rates potentially peaking at 5.25 percent this year. “Persistent inflation pressures are likely to reinforce a hawkish policy stance, supporting our forecast for an additional 50 basis points (bps) of tightening in 2026,” Deepali Bhargava, regional head of research for ING Asia-Pacific, noted in a commentary. “Political uncertainty remains a key downside risk, potentially delaying reforms, dampening growth, and sustaining downward pressure on the peso,” Bhargava added.

Female debt collector found dead in Leyte. TACLOBAN CITY — A 21-year-old debt collector was found dead on Sunday, August 9, at Sitio Ilaya, Barangay Matlang, Isabel, Leyte. The victim, identified only as alias “Rose”, had been reported missing since August 3. She was a resident of Isabel and a native of Matag-ob, Leyte. The suspect, identified as “Paulo”, 20 years old, a habal-habal driver and resident of Isabel, Leyte, voluntarily surrendered himself at the Isabel Municipal Police Station. He admitted responsibility for the victim’s death. The suspect led authorities to the crime scene. There, officers found the victim lying face down in an advanced state of decomposition. Initial investigation revealed that on August 3, the suspect persuaded the victim to accompany him, claiming he needed to pay monthly dues at the CARD-Isabel Branch where she worked as a collector. They traveled together on his motorcycle. Upon reaching the mountainous portion of Sitio Matlang, they got off and walked toward what the suspect said was a debtor’s home. Shortly after, the victim became suspicious, which led to an argument. During the altercation, the suspect strangled her, causing her death on the spot. The suspect is currently in the custody of the Isabel Municipal Police Station, awaiting the appropriate filing of charges.#

Peralta cops five medals in Asian weightlifting. Jhodie Peralta delivered five medals in two divisions for Team Philippines at the Asian Youth & Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan on Sunday, Aug. 9. The Zamboanga City standout captured two gold and one silver medal in the youth women’s 53 kg division, as well as one gold and one silver in the junior women’s 53 kg to add more medals in the Team PH’s war chest. She ruled the youth class with a total lift of 188 kgs after posting 86 kg for the gold medal in snatch, and 102 kg for silver in clean & jerk. In the junior category, she topped the snatch with 86 kg, but finished fourth in clean & jerk with 102 kg to settle for the silver in total with 188 kgs, just one kg lighter than eventual champion Natcha Kaewnoi of Thailand. The Filipino lifters now have 13 gold, nine silver and five bronze medals after a massive haul on Saturday, Aug. 8, where five lifters collected eight gold, five silver and four bronze medals. Still scheduled to see action are world youth champion Albert Ian Delos Santos (men’s 70kg), Jea Mae Palagtiw (women’s 69kg) and Rhianne Cabalida (women’s 77kg), and junior athletes Rosalinda Faustino (women’s 57kg) and Mango Prince David Tarro (men’s 65kg).

Chinese Ambassador: Let’s talk. There are probably easier places to discuss the state of Philippines-China relations than in the middle of a food festival. Then again, perhaps there are few better ones. This writer caught up with Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan at Asia Society Philippines’ Asian Eats 2026 held at the EDSA Shangri-La mall over the weekend, where embassies and cultural institutions had gathered around one of diplomacy’s more agreeable subjects: food. Asian Eats is built around the idea that cuisine can be a form of cultural diplomacy, bringing people closer through something as seemingly ordinary as what we eat. This year, with the Philippines serving as ASEAN Chair, the festival also placed particular emphasis on Southeast Asia and the region’s interconnected food cultures. Jing clearly enjoyed the premise. “It’s about the people-to-people culture,” he told me. “People share culture with each other.” There was something refreshingly simple about the way he put it: you do not need a common language to appreciate another country. Sometimes food, dance, martial arts or simple curiosity will do. And apparently, the ambassador has been doing quite a bit of eating his way around the Philippines. In the roughly eight months since arriving in the country, Jing shared he had already traveled to 20 provinces. His rule when visiting somewhere new is simple: ask where to find the best local Filipino food. “Not Chinese,” he emphasized, laughing. Naturally, I asked what had won him over. Sinigang, it turns out, has a fan in the Chinese Embassy. Food, of course, was doing the heavy lifting that day. Asian Eats, Asia Society Philippines’ flagship culinary and cultural diplomacy festival, brought embassies and communities together through the region’s food and traditions. With the Philippines serving as ASEAN Chair, this year’s edition included a special ASEAN Showcase highlighting Southeast Asia’s shared influences and distinct culinary identities. The Chinese Embassy’s participation went beyond the table, with dance and Shaolin Kung Fu performances. A highlight was Chef LV Wei’s cooking demonstration of Chongqing spicy chicken. The dish came with its own history lesson. Chili peppers, now essential to Sichuan and Chongqing cuisine, originated in the Americas and reached China via the Philippines along maritime trade routes. By the 17th century, they had taken root in southwestern China and eventually became integral to the region’s cooking. Chef LV brought that journey full circle by using Philippine-grown chilies for his Chongqing spicy chicken. There was something wonderfully appropriate about it: a Chinese chef in Manila preparing a Chongqing classic with Philippine-grown chilies, an ingredient whose own history was shaped by trade and exchange across borders. That exchange was happening all around us, as guests moved between country offerings, performances and cooking demonstrations, encountering unfamiliar cultures in the most accessible way. It was a fitting setting for my conversation with Jing—and an unexpected entry point into a far more complicated subject. Because enjoying each other’s food is easy. Managing one of the region’s most consequential bilateral relationships is considerably harder. Philippines-China relations remain strained by competing claims and increasingly serious encounters in the West Philippine Sea. So I asked Jing the obvious question: what can people-to-people exchanges really accomplish when relations between governments are under this much pressure? His answer was that disagreements need not consume everything else. “Although we have some disputes, we can manage. We can talk,” he said. The two countries, he said, should continue focusing on trade, culture and exchanges that produce tangible benefits for ordinary Filipinos and Chinese. That distinction—between having differences and allowing those differences to define the entire relationship—became the thread running through the rest of our conversation. Jing is particularly interested in the economic side of his posting. Clean energy was the first sector he mentioned where he saw opportunities for greater cooperation. He pointed to electric vehicles, solar projects and waste-to-energy technology, before moving on to artificial intelligence, the digital economy and agricultural technology. He also wants China buying more from the Philippines. His larger argument is that economic cooperation requires predictability. Businesses are more likely to invest, he said, when they are confident that political deterioration will not suddenly place their investments at risk. What he hopes to see is what he called a “positive interaction”: more trade and people-to-people exchanges creating greater confidence to manage political differences, and more stable political relations in turn encouraging further business. The alternative, in his description, is a vicious cycle. There is, of course, an important caveat here. Economic opportunity cannot make legitimate questions of sovereignty, maritime rights and national security disappear. Nor should cultural diplomacy be mistaken for a substitute for the difficult work of statecraft. But diplomacy has never required countries to agree on everything before they speak to each other. And Jing seems determined to get people speaking again. He shared that political dialogue between Manila and Beijing, after a period of stalled engagement, has resumed, with five rounds of talks already held this year. He described his own working relations with Philippine officials as “very smooth,” saying he had met with nearly 20 Cabinet-level officials as well as heads of law-enforcement agencies. “Our door is always open,” he said. One area, however, remains particularly difficult. Military-to-military exchanges, Jing acknowledged, have effectively stopped. He hopes to see those channels restored as well. “Let’s calm down. Let’s talk to each other,” he said, stressing that difficult issues should be managed while both countries continue working in areas where cooperation remains possible. Whether Manila and Beijing can actually create that virtuous cycle is another matter entirely. There are disputes between the Philippines and China that cannot be resolved over dinner, however good the food may be. Recent events in the West Philippine Sea are a reminder that cultural warmth and geopolitical friction can exist simultaneously. Perhaps that is precisely why encounters like Asian Eats are worth paying attention to. Earlier this year, Jing spoke before Asia Society Philippines about restarting political dialogue, expanding people-to-people exchanges and deepening economic cooperation, while also acknowledging maritime disputes among the major challenges confronting bilateral relations. At Asian Eats, those people-to-people exchanges took on a much simpler form. Jing put it rather neatly when we first started talking: people from different countries can still like each other’s culture. That will not solve the West Philippine Sea. But diplomacy is rarely built from a single grand gesture. Sometimes it begins by preserving enough space for another conversation. And, apparently, a bowl of sinigang.

Damaged classrooms climb to 3,924 due to ‘Maymay,’ habagat — DepEd. The number of classrooms damaged by the combined effects of Tropical Cyclone “Maymay” and the southwest monsoon or “habagat” has climbed to 3,924, up from 2,424 reported a day earlier, the Department of Education (DepEd) said on Monday, Aug. 10. Based on DepEd’s latest situation report as of 8 a.m. on Aug. 10, 2,355 classrooms sustained minor damage, 818 had major damage, while 751 were totally damaged. “As of today, the combined effects of Southwest Monsoon and former Tropical Cyclone Maymay left damages on 722 schools—affecting 751 totally damaged, 818 major damaged, and 2,355 minor damaged classrooms,” the agency reported. As such, DepEd reported non-infrastructure losses, including 5,368 chairs, 380 units of ICT equipment, and 6,227 learning materials, which affected teaching and learning across the affected regions. “Fifty-two schools are currently being used as evacuation centers, with 239 classrooms being used to accommodate 1,057 families,” it added. Emergency measures activated Per DepEd, it has activated measures to ensure learning continuity amid class disruptions caused by heavy rains from the southwest monsoon or “habagat” in Metro Manila and several provinces, with schools and field offices reminded to implement its Education in Emergencies framework to protect learners, teachers, and school personnel. The agency issued the reminder following Memorandum Circular No. 123 from the Office of the President, which directed schools in affected areas to shift to alternative learning modes on Monday, Aug. 10, unless otherwise ordered by local chief executives. The education department said the prevailing weather conditions underscore the need for schools to apply the 4H protocol, or Hinto, Hinga, Hinay, and Hayo, when making decisions on learning delivery, taking into account safety, learner readiness, available resources, and conditions on the ground. DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara said the policy seeks to help schools respond to disruptions while ensuring the safety of learners and teachers and allowing learning to continue when conditions permit. “Kapag malakas ang ulan, baha ang daan, o may risk sa safety ng learners at teachers, hindi puwedeng one-size-fits-all ang decision (When the rain is heavy, roads are flooded, or there is a risk to the safety of learners and teachers, decisions cannot take a one-size-fits-all approach),” he said in a statement. “Kailangan malinaw ang batayan: ligtas ba, kaya ba, at anong klaseng learning support ang angkop? Iyan ang layunin ng 4H framework — gabayan ang schools kung kailan tutuloy, kailan babagalan, kailan hihinga, at kailan kailangang huminto muna (There must be clear bases: Is it safe? Is it feasible? And what kind of learning support is appropriate? That is the purpose of the 4H framework, to guide schools on when to proceed, when to slow down, when to take a breather, and when they need to stop temporarily).” DepEd said that under the 4H framework, Hinto calls for a temporary halt to academic activities when conditions are unsafe, while Hinga gives learners, teachers, and school personnel time to recover from disruptions through well-being checks, psychosocial support, and light activities without regular academic requirements. Under Hinay, learning may continue through adjusted, teacher-supervised synchronous or asynchronous modes, while Hayo signals the safe resumption of regular learning. The agency added that areas that shifted to asynchronous or alternative learning modes due to the rains may be classified under Hinay, provided that learners and teachers are safe and academic requirements are adjusted accordingly. The education department stressed that schools should not force regular academic activities during emergencies when conditions pose safety risks or significant stress. Learning should instead be adjusted according to risks, accessibility, and the well-being of learners and personnel. Likewise, DepEd told schools to coordinate with local government units, disaster risk reduction and management offices, and field offices in determining the appropriate level of learning continuity.

Machine operator reported missing after being swept away by floodwater in Quezon. CANDELARIA, Quezon- A 32-year-old machine operator was reportedly swept away by the strong current of water while crossing the spillway aboard a tricycle on Sunday morning, Aug. 9, in Barangay Masalukot 1, this town Victim Raymark, married and a resident of Sitio Labak, Brgy. Mayabobo, here. The investigation disclosed that at about 1:50 a.m., the victim was traveling from Barangay Masalukot 1, and was crossing the spillway heading towards Barangay Mayabobo when the tricycle he was driving was swept away by the river's strong current, which had overflowed onto the roadway due to continuous rains. The floodwaters swept away both the victim and the vehicle. Police said that as of reporting time, the search and rescue operations are ongoing by joint police, municipal disaster risk reduction and management office (MDRRMO), and local barangay officials to locate the victim and recover the tricycle.

'Edi Magalit ka': SunKissed Lola finds love in the little fights. Filipinos have always had a soft spot for love songs, tunes about falling in love, getting hurt, missing someone, or simply finding comfort in another person. It is familiar territory for many musicians. But how do you make a love song feel fresh? For SunKissed Lola, the answer is to keep it simple. Instead of grand declarations or sweeping heartbreak, the band looks at something more ordinary: the little fights, tampuhan, stubborn moments, and the inevitable making up that come with being in love. That is the idea behind “Edi Magalit Ka,” the band’s new single. It is still very much a love song, but this time, SunKissed Lola takes a lighter and more playful approach. “It’s a song about relationships,” vocalist Laura Lacbain says. “Hindi maiiwasan ang away sa relationship, pero hindi pa rin mawawala ang love. Susuyuin pa rin sa huli.” Vocalist and guitarist Alvin “Bino” Serito calls it a “loving anthem,” built around the idea that even when couples get upset with each other, the love does not simply disappear. “Even if you’re mad with your special someone, at the end of the day, they’re still your favorite person to come home to,” he says. The song actually began in 2021, but the original version was more prideful. As the band worked on it, the lyrics became softer and more open. “No one has to win,” Bino says. “I will always choose the relationship over the argument.” Even the title plays with that idea. “Edi magalit ka” may sound dismissive at first, but the band gives the familiar phrase a more affectionate meaning. “The title was intriguing in itself,” Laura says. “You will be curious. Pwedeng i-send sa jowa. You really need to listen to the song to understand the context.” The same simplicity carries into the music. What started as an acoustic piece eventually became a warm, laid-back arrangement. The band kept things straightforward, allowing the lyrics to take the lead. “We all united to make it sound laid-back, simple, and we wanted to highlight the lyrics of the song,” bassist Danj Quimson says. “For this one, we made it simple for the audience,” Bino adds. “We made it magaan sa tainga.” SunKissed Lola is still singing about love. This time, though, they are not looking at the big romantic moments. They are looking at the arguments, the tampuhan, and the moments when two people have to decide whether to hold on to their pride or fix things. Sometimes, that is where the real love story is. “Edi Magalit Ka” is out now on all major streaming platforms.

Ilocos Sur orders evacuations as 'habagat' batters province. VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — The Ilocos Sur provincial government ordered the immediate evacuation of residents in flood-, landslide-, and coastal-hazard prone areas as heavy rains from the enhanced southwest monsoon, or 'hHabagat', battered the province over the weekend. Classes in public and private schools and work in government offices were also suspended Monday, Aug. 10, under Executive Order No. 25. The order requires local government units (LGUs) to maintain 24/7 emergency operations centers and conduct mandatory evacuations in high-risk communities. As of 1 p.m. Sunday, 72 families or 220 individuals from Vigan City and the towns of Narvacan, Santiago, and Santo Domingo had evacuated to designated centers. The Provincial Diaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) said the enhanced habagat had affected 190 families or 569 individuals in 27 barangays as of Sunday morning. Including the effects of tropical cyclones Luis, Dolphin, and Maymay, a total of 661 families or 1,976 individuals in 92 barangays have been affected. Flooding, landslides, and overflowing rivers were reported in several areas. Two fishermen were also rescued after encountering trouble in San Esteban. Authorities reported 106 partially damaged houses, with losses reaching P3.03 million in agriculture, P225,670 in livestock, and P87.73 million in infrastructure. Local government units (LGUs) and the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD)have provided evacuees with food packs, hot meals, and other essential supplies. Authorities urged residents in vulnerable areas to remain alert and immediately comply with evacuation orders as heavy rains continue.

128th birth anniversary of ex-senator Lorenzo Tañada, Sr. commemorated in Quezon. GUMACA, Quezon- A fervent tribute on the 128th birth anniversary of Senator Lorenzo M. Tañada, Sr, was held here on Monday, Aug. 10. Representatives from various sectors participated at the formal unveiling of a statue of the esteemed statesman, blessing, and flower offering ceremony was held at Nava Boulevard in this town. The event was led by Mayor Webster Letargo, the fifth generation of the Tañada family, and former fourth district Representative Erin Tañada, the grandson, and his relatives, members of the Sangguniang Bayan, local government staff, and various socio-civic groups. Tañada could be remembered as more than just a steadfast pillar of justice. "Ka Tanny" stood as a courageous bulwark and defender of our democracy. Amidst the reign of dictatorship and the trampling of human rights, he fearlessly took to the streets to fight for the restoration of the Filipino people's voice and freedom. His life serves as a clear reminder: democracy is not merely inherited; it must be constantly fought for and protected. Today, his commitment is reignited to uphold press freedom, social justice, and the true power of the people—legacies forged through the time and energy of the great "Grand Old Man of Philippine Politics."

LANDBANK marks 63 years with global honors for innovation, inclusion, and dev’t impact. As LANDBANK celebrates its 63rd anniversary, the Bank continues to earn prestigious international and local recognition for advancing financial inclusion, digital transformation, sustainable finance, and nation-building. Global banking and digital leadership Among its most notable distinctions, LANDBANK was named Philippines' Best Retail Bank at the prestigious Euromoney Awards for Excellence, one of the banking industry's most respected awards programs. The recognition affirms LANDBANK's continued efforts to make banking more accessible, affordable, and convenient for millions of Filipinos. Through innovations such as zero-fee government payment transactions, free InstaPay fund transfers, the LANDBANK Mobile Banking App, and the LANDBANKasama program, the Bank has helped bring financial services closer to underserved and remote communities while driving broader adoption of digital payments nationwide. LANDBANK also played a key role in the government's fuel subsidy and targeted cash assistance programs, leveraging its extensive network and digital capabilities to efficiently deliver financial support to priority sectors. Further underscoring its digital leadership, the International Finance Awards recognized LANDBANK for Fastest Growing Digital Banking Services in the Philippines for 2026, highlighting its commitment to delivering secure, convenient, and customer-centered banking solutions. "These recognitions affirm LANDBANK's vital role in advancing financial inclusion, supporting key sectors of the economy, and helping drive the National Government's agenda for inclusive and sustainable growth. As the Bank marks its 63rd anniversary, these recognitions inspire us to build on this momentum by delivering greater value to the Filipino people through responsive, innovative, and development-oriented banking," Finance Secretary and LANDBANK Chair Frederick D. Go said. Development banking leadership LANDBANK's development-focused initiatives likewise gained global recognition. At the Global Banking & Finance Review Awards, LANDBANK was named Best Development Bank and Best Agri Business Bank in the Philippines, affirming its leadership in supporting sectors that drive countryside development and economic growth. LANDBANK President and CEO Lynette V. Ortiz was likewise recognized as the country’s Banking CEO of the Year. Meanwhile, the Pan Finance Awards honored LANDBANK as Most Innovative Rural Development Bank and Agricultural Financing Partner of the Year, recognizing the Bank's sustained support for farmers, fishers, agrarian reform beneficiaries (ARBs), micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and local government units (LGUs). Through programs such as AGRISENSO Plus, ASCEND, and LIFTING MSMEs, the Bank continues to expand access to financing that helps farmers, fishers, and entrepreneurs grow their businesses and participate more actively in the formal economy. Further affirming her leadership in advancing LANDBANK's development mandate, Ortiz was recognized by the International Finance Awards as Best Woman CEO in Banking in the Philippines for 2026. “These recognitions belong to every LANDBANKer whose hard work and dedication bring our mission to life each day. They affirm that our efforts to deliver accessible and inclusive financial services are creating real value for the Filipinos and communities we serve. As we mark 63 years, we remain committed to empowering communities and enabling opportunities that help build a better future for every Filipino,” said LANDBANK President and CEO Ortiz. Sustainable finance leadership Beyond financial inclusion and development banking, LANDBANK also gained international recognition for supporting the country's sustainability agenda. At The Asset Triple A Sustainable Finance Awards, the Bank received the Renewable Energy Deal of the Year – Hydro award for its role in financing major renewable energy projects that strengthen energy security, enhance grid reliability, and support the country's clean energy transition. LANDBANK's renewable energy portfolio includes financing for Prime Infrastructure Capital Inc.'s sustainability initiatives, Citicore Renewable Energy Corporation's solar power and battery energy storage projects, and an ₱800-million facility for Archipelago Renewables Corporation (ARC) to deploy hybrid renewable energy-powered microgrids in underserved communities in Palawan. These investments expand access to cleaner, more reliable energy while advancing the country's long-term energy security and sustainability goals. Advancing nation-building Taken together, these honors affirm a development mandate that has guided LANDBANK for more than six decades — one measured not in industry recognition alone, but in the farmers financed, the communities reached, and the opportunities opened for ordinary Filipinos. As it marks 63 years of service, LANDBANK remains steadfast in driving innovation, sustainability, and customer-centered banking — helping build a more inclusive, resilient, and prosperous Philippines.

'Kuliglig' becomes widespread alternative transport in flooded areas in Pangasinan. CALASIAO, Pangasinan — Farm machinery, locally known as “kuliglig”, has become an alternative mode of transportation in some flood-affected areas here. The type of vehicles is currently being used to transport residents through flooded roads. " Marami na sa jeep o traysikel ayaw na magsakay sa amin kapag ganyan na baha at lampas tuhod na (Many of the jeepneys and tricycles refuse to take passengers whenever the floodwater reaches beyond knee-high)", a commuter said. The minimum fare for the kuliglig rides is reportedly ₱20 per passenger. The situation reflects how residents are adapting to difficult travel conditions as floodwaters affect mobility in low-lying communities. Residents here are advised to exercise caution when using flooded roads, particularly in areas where water levels are deep. Meanwhile, kuliglig operators, many of them farmers, are also benefiting from the increased demand for transport amid the flooding. Some farmers reportedly earn thousands of pesos in a day by using their farm machinery to ferry passengers through flood-affected roads. The kuliglig has become a practical lifeline for residents—and an unexpected livelihood opportunity for farmers during the flooding.

3 arrested for oil pilferage in Batangas. BAUAN, Batangas-Three individuals were apprehended for oil pilferage on Sunday evening in Barangay San Pedro, this town, Aug. 9. Arrested were Junjun, 19, single, helper, of San Pedro, Bauan; Baldwin, 29, driver, married, of Soro-Soro Ibaba, Batangas City, and Norben, 43, single, of San Pedro, Bauan. At about 8 p.m., Bauan police received a cellular phone call from a concerned citizen regarding an alleged illegal activity of oil pilferage and a foul smell of petroleum products emanating from a compound in the said village. The informant expressed concern that fire might break out because of this. The lawmen responded to conduct validation and surveillance. Upon arrival at the said compound, foul smell of petroleum products was observed, and in plain view, the lawmen saw Junjun in the act of spilling petroleum products on the floor while Baldwin was driving an Isuzu Dropside Truck, with license plate number DXZ680, and Norben was a passenger. Upon investigation, the suspects admitted that they were members of a crew involved in oil pilferage, and not a single document nor a permit could be presented by the suspects to dispute his. A bulk container with petroleum products and two pails of petroleum products, and the truck were seized for proper documentation. An appropriate complaint is being prepared by the police.

Ayala launches ACX Retail to bring global brands to Philippines. ACX Holdings Corp., the retail investment unit of local conglomerate Ayala Corp., has launched a specialized retail operating platform to scale international consumer brands in the country, aiming to capture a larger share of resilient domestic consumer spending. In a statement, Ayala said the newly formed entity, ACX Retail, will function as an operational launchpad designed to introduce, roll out, and manage overseas fashion, lifestyle, and specialty retail concepts nationwide. The strategic move highlights how major Philippine conglomerates are doubling down on consumer-driven growth as private consumption continues to serve as a primary engine of the domestic economy. By leveraging Ayala’s extensive real estate footprint, logistics infrastructure, and consumer data ecosystem, ACX Retail plans to mitigate operational friction for foreign entrants seeking to establish a long-term presence in Southeast Asia's fast-growing retail market. Earlier this year, ACX Holdings established joint ventures with several prominent global retailers, including Australian value retailer Anko, Thailand-based wholesale operator Makro, United Arab Emirates grocery chain Spinneys, and South Korea’s apparel label Musinsa Standard. ACX Retail will serve as the dedicated execution arm for these ventures, with a focus on adapting foreign business models to local consumer preferences while scaling store rollouts nationwide. “At ACX, our role is to help exceptional brands succeed in the Philippine market by combining their strengths with our understanding of local consumers, our retail capabilities, and the reach of the Ayala ecosystem,” Mark Uy, head of corporate strategy and business development at Ayala, said. He added that these commercial partnerships align with the group's broader mandate to expand consumer choice while sharpening the overall competitiveness of the domestic retail industry. Executives at the company stressed that brand acquisition will remain selective, targeting international concepts with proven commercial viability and distinct brand equity tailored to evolving middle-class demographics in the Philippines. “Filipino consumers are increasingly looking for quality, relevance, and differentiated experiences,” said Rohit Kohli, chief retail officer at ACX Retail. “Our focus is to bring the right global concepts to the Philippines and build them into sustainable businesses that create long-term value.” Through the launch of ACX Retail, Ayala is broadening its consumer-facing portfolio beyond traditional shopping mall development into active brand operations and merchandise management. The enterprise aims to position itself as the preferred local joint-venture partner for multinational retail corporations seeking sustainable expansion in the Philippine market.

Filipino seniors remain vulnerable to poverty despite social safety nets—PIDS. Many older Filipinos remain at risk of falling into poverty despite not being officially classified as poor, highlighting gaps in pension coverage and the need for a broader measure of economic vulnerability, according to state-run policy think tank Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS). In a statement on Monday, Aug. 10, PIDS said a recent study found that while only 7.8 percent of senior citizens were classified as poor in 2023, 24 percent were vulnerable to falling into poverty. The disparity suggests that poverty rates alone may overlook many older Filipinos who face economic insecurity and could benefit from social protection programs. The official poverty threshold determines whether households can afford a minimum basket of food and non-food needs at a given point in time, but does not measure the likelihood that households just above the threshold could fall into poverty because of economic or health-related shocks. For older Filipinos, whose incomes are often fixed while healthcare needs tend to increase with age, measuring vulnerability alongside poverty could provide a more comprehensive picture of their economic situation. The risk was even higher among senior citizens living in mixed-generation households, particularly those with children, where vulnerability reached nearly 45 percent despite relatively low poverty rates. PIDS supervising research specialist Deanne Lorraine Cabalfin said older Filipinos also experience economic vulnerability differently depending on their circumstances. “Older women living alone rely heavily on remittances for income, while older men living alone are the most asset-poor. Older households also spend a larger share of their income on food and healthcare, leaving many economically fragile despite not being classified as poor,” Cabalfin said. Women are particularly vulnerable as they often reach old age with fewer savings and weaker pension coverage, while disability, social isolation and Indigenous identity can further compound disadvantages. Pension coverage also remains a major gap, with 42 percent of Filipinos aged 60 and above receiving no pension. Nearly one-third of Social Security System (SSS) pensioners receive less than ₱3,000 per month, while the government’s social pension provides only ₱1,000 monthly. The social pension program also faces targeting challenges, with some eligible senior citizens excluded while some non-indigent beneficiaries are included. Cabalfin called for the regular measurement of vulnerability alongside poverty to ensure that social protection programs better reflect the actual economic risks faced by older Filipinos. “Kailangan nating regular na sukatin ang vulnerability, kasama ng poverty, para tugma ang program targeting sa tunay na risk (We need to regularly measure vulnerability alongside poverty so that the program targeting reflects the real risks people face),” Cabalfin said. Based on the findings, she also recommended a fiscally sustainable expansion of social pensions to widen protection for older Filipinos. - Danielle T. Bayani

Bangsamoro Federalist Party launches bid for seats in BARMM parliament. DAVAO CITY – The Bangsamoro Federalist Party has formally launched over the weekend its campaign for the first Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) Parliamentary Elections next month. According to the BFP, at least 54, 000 supporters have gathered in different parts of the region for the simultaneous region-wide campaign kickoff in Basilan, Cotabato City, Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte and the Special Geographic Area. The group said that the Lanao del Sur had the most number of people who joined the activity with 17,000 followed by the event in Basilan and Cotabato City with 10, 000 people respectively. Founded in March this year, the BFP is mostly composed of the current BARMM used to be affiliated with the United Bangsamoro Justice Party(UBJP), the political party of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front. (MILF). Recently, several notable local government officials have moved to BFP from UBJP, including Cotabato City Mayor Mohammad Ali “Bruce” Matabalao. Matabalo resigned from UBJP in June 2026, and joined BFP as first vice president, along with half of the city council and other officials; Maguindanao del Sur Rep. Esmael “Toto” Mangudadatu and other local officials. BFP is currently led by BARMM Member of the Parliament Tomanda Antok, who used to lead the planning committee of the UBJP. Antok said that BFP is now the most dominant party in the region as about 90% of the local government officials and even down to barangay councils in BARMM have already joined the group. “Of the 11 mayors in the province of Tawi-Tawi, 10 of them took oath before the Bangsamoro Federalist Party. Also in Basilan, 10 of 11 mayors swore before the Bangsamoro Federalist Party,” Andtok told the crowd in Cotabato City. While 22 of 24 mayors in Maguindanao del Sur and 12 of 13 mayors in Maguindanao del Norte have already joined the BFP, he added. However, Antok did not specify how many of 39 mayors and barangay officials have already joined the BFP. While lawyer Naguib Sinarimbo, who is also a BARMM Member of the Parliament, serves as the Cotabato City Chapter President and the group’s spokesperson. The group is advocating for transparency, good governance , inclusive development and peacebuilding in the region. Both BFP and UBJP are among the most dominant parties that will participate in the first parliamentary elections on September 14. Ten other regional parliamentary political parties have also been accredited for the polls. Commission on Elections (COMELEC) chairperson George Edwin Garcia announced last week that the agency is “95% ready” for the region’s first-ever polls. The 45-day campaign period commenced on July 30 with 631 candidates and nominees vying for 80 seats. In the upcoming historic election, BARMM voters will elect 80 Members of Parliament (MPs) , one regional parliamentary political party (RPPP), one district representative, and six sectoral representatives – two for settler communities, one each for women, youth, Ulama and traditional leaders. According to the Comelec, the two other sectoral seats reserved for Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples (NMIPs) – will be chosen through tribal assemblies ahead of the September 14 polls. (Keith Bacongco)

‘The fruit of Alas Women’s labor’ – Minowa on PH’s historic silver finish in SEA V Cup. It seems Alas Pilipinas is in good hands under coach Taka Minowa following its historic silver medal finish at the expense of Indonesia, 25-13, 23-25, 25-19, 33-31 , in the 2026 SEA V Cup Leg 2 last Sunday, Aug. 9. But for the newly-minted Alas mentor, it was the hard work of each squad member, including their mother club and the whole coaching staff, that was key to their recent feat. “I believe this moment is not only about the players who are with us in the national team pool,” Minowa, husband of one of the country’s top hitters Jaja Santiago (Sachi Minowa), wrote on his social media post. “It is the result of the hard work of so many players, coaches, and clubs who have continued to develop and make Philippine volleyball more competitive over the years,” he added. The 34-year-old tactician also credited all the players and coaches – from school to the professional ranks – whose contributions helped them build the current level of Philippine women’s volleyball. “I hope everyone can be proud of the players and coaches who gave their time, effort, and heart to this team,” he concluded. “This achievement is the result of everyone’s hard work, and I’m very grateful to be part of this journey with all of you.” Prior to their silver finish, the Nationals went winless in the first leg before bouncing back in Leg 2 where their twin victories was highlighted by a 2-25, 25-23, 25-21, 25-22 upset win over perennial Southeast Asian Games podium finisher Vietnam. Apart from the team’s feat, the country also secured individual honors with Eya Laure being named as one of the Best Outside Spikers while Alyssa Solomon bagged the Best Opposite Spiker plum. “Para sa Bayan!!” Laure captioned on her social media post of her photo carrying her award and the 1st runner-up trophy. Month later it will a much tougher task ahead for the two Filipina awardees, alongside spikers Bella Belen, Angel Canino, Vanie Gandler, and Shai Nitura, to list a few – as they named as part of the Alas pool for the coming Aichi-Nagoya 20th Asian Games in Japan. Minowa is also appointed as the podium-hungry crew’s head coach in the quadrennial meet, where the Philippines, a two-time fourth place finisher in 1962 and 1966 editions, is bracketed in Group B together with reigning champion China and Kazakhstan.

Police confiscate 858 illegal firearms in Western Visayas. ILOILO CITY—The Police Regional Office (PRO-6) was able to confiscate 858 illegal firearms across Western Visayas over a two-month period. Brigadier General Randulf T. Tuaño, PRO-6 regional director, personally inspected the firearms that were voluntarily surrendered between May 15 to July 31, 2026. The recovery of the illegal firearms was part of Project Restrict, Track, and Turn-in or PROJECT R.T.T. “Bawat baril na boluntaryong isinusuko ay isang baril na hindi na posibleng mapunta sa maling kamay. Para sa amin, buhay na maaaring mailigtas iyon at insidenteng maaaring maiwasan (Every firearm voluntarily surrendered is one that can no longer fall into the wrong hands. For us, that represents a life potentially saved and an incident potentially averted),” said Tuaño. “Mas mabuting maagap tayong kumilos at makipagtulungan sa komunidad kaysa hintayin pang magamit ang mga baril sa krimen (It is better to take proactive measures and collaborate with the community than to wait until these firearms are used in the commission of a crime),” added Tuaño. Colonel Adrian Accolador, chief of PRO-6’s Regional Division Operation, said that Iloilo Police Provincial Office (Iloilo PPO) had the most number of retrieval with 410 firearms. Antique PPO ranked second with 129 firearms retrieved while Aklan PPO ranked third with 97 firearms recovered. There were also 95 firearms recovered by Capiz PPO, 59 by Iloilo City Police Office, 57 by Regional Mobile Force Battalion (RMFB-6), and 11 by Guimaras PPO.

Lacson: DPWH to halt ongoing projects in Taguig, forfeit banned reclaimed areas. All unpermitted reclaimed areas in Taguig City—whether belonging to the local government or to private individuals or entities—are subject to forfeiture in favor of the national government. Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson disclosed this on Monday, August 10 saying this was made clear by officials of the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) to him and his staff, as well as with officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH). “All reclaimed areas that did not apply and secure permits from PRA are subject to forfeiture in favor of the national government. There is no distinction, whether those reclaimed areas belong to the LGU of Taguig or are titled under private individuals or corporate entities,” Lacson said. Moreover, the PRA and DPWH have agreed that the latter will begin issuing cease-and-desist orders covering ongoing slope protection and mitigation projects in that area, following the discovery of 32 anomalous and suspected ghost projects in Taguig. Lacson also pointed out that the denials made by Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano in his Facebook Live broadcasts are contradicted by the facts established so far by him and his team, and validated by the concerned agencies. “In sum, Sen. Cayetano’s denials on his FB Live postings all run counter to the facts as established so far, not only by my team, but validated by PRA and DPWH and Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) in their earlier statements,” he said. Lacson also said the Office of the Ombudsman will soon initiate its fact-finding investigation into his and his team’s disclosures on the anomalous projects in Taguig City. This was after Lacson and his team turned over to the Ombudsman all the records and documents culled from the General Appropriations Acts (GAA) and official government websites, including the relevant photos. “In due time, the Ombudsman will issue subpoenas duces tecum and ad testificandum to DPWH and private witnesses after we also turned them over with their affidavits to the Ombudsman,” he said.

AREIT to acquire Fairmont Raffles, major malls in ₱20-billion property swap. AREIT Inc., the real estate investment trust sponsored by Ayala Land Inc., agreed to acquire two luxury hotels and five shopping malls from its parent developer in a transaction valued at ₱19.95 billion. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange, AREIT said the property injection consists of a ₱17.33 billion property-for-share swap alongside a ₱2.62 billion direct cash transaction. Under the equity arrangement, Ayala Land and its subsidiaries—Capitol Central Commercial Ventures Corp., Makati Cornerstone Leasing Corp., Bay City Commercial Ventures Corp., and North Triangle Hotel Ventures Inc.—will receive 462.48 million AREIT shares priced at ₱37.48 apiece. The asset transfer includes Glorietta 4 and Ayala Malls Circuit in Makati, Ayala Malls Capitol Central in Bacolod, Ayala Malls Cloverleaf in Quezon City, the New World Makati Hotel, and the Seda Vertis North hotel. In a separate cash deal, AREIT will purchase the Fairmont Raffles Hotel Makati from ALI Makati Hotel and Residences Inc. The transaction remains subject to approval by AREIT shareholders at a special meeting scheduled for Sept. 23, 2026, as well as final regulatory clearances. AREIT will structure the mall acquisitions under direct lease contracts, matching its existing office properties to directly recognize retail rental earnings. The hotel assets will operate under hybrid master leases combining fixed base rent with variable returns tied to operational revenues, giving the trust a balance of guaranteed yields and performance upside. The announcement follows a strong operational showing in the first six months of the year. AREIT generated ₱7.7 billion in total revenue during the first half of 2026, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization rose 34% to ₱5.8 billion. Net income, excluding fair-value adjustments on investment properties, surged 36 percent to ₱5.8 billion, driven by full-period contributions from acquisitions made over the past two years alongside steady occupancy across its legacy portfolio. Assets under management reached ₱159.4 billion during the period, spanning commercial office towers, shopping centers, hotels, and industrial sites. The board approved a second-quarter cash dividend of ₱0.63 per share, payable on Sept. 9, 2026, to stockholders of record as of Aug. 25, 2026. The company previously received regulatory approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission on June 26, 2026, for an earlier asset swap involving Ayala Land and Summerhill Commercial Ventures Corp. (James A. Loyola)

414 areas remain flooded as ‘habagat rains’ continue, OCD says. Flooding persisted in 414 areas across several regions on Monday, Aug. 10, as the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) continued to bring rain, according to the Office of Civil Defense (OCD). Central Luzon (Region 3) recorded the highest number of flooded areas at 227, followed by Calabarzon (Region 4A) with 88, Ilocos (Region 1) with 65, and Mimaropa (region 4B) with 34. The Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) and Western Visayas (Region 6) reported no flooded areas although residents in these areas were affected by habagat rains. OCD information officer Diego Mariano said local government disaster response teams continued to assist affected communities, including residents who may have become stranded by rising floodwaters. “As for the flooded areas, there are people who may have been trapped on rooftops. The rescue responders of local government units, particularly those from the local DRRM offices, continue to be deployed,” Mariano said. The OCD said responders from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), and Philippine National Police (PNP) were also on standby to augment local responders if needed. “They are on standby once the responders already dispatched to their respective local government units are not enough,” Mariano said. Meanwhile, the OCD recorded power interruptions in 65 cities and municipalities but electricity had been restored in 52 others while 13 others remained without electricity. Calabarzon accounted for eight areas with ongoing power interruptions, followed by Ilocos Region with four, and CAR with one. Water supply also remained interrupted in three cities and municipalities. Two were in Calabarzon and one was in Ilocos Region. Mariano said residents should act early when authorities advise evacuation, particularly as more rain was expected in the coming days. “From the OCD, our advice to our fellow citizens is to continue to cooperate. Once authorities tell us to evacuate or advise us to prepare, we should follow them to avoid additional casualties,” he said. He said residents should not wait until floodwaters or landslide risks become immediately life-threatening before leaving their homes. “This is because people sometimes evacuate only when the ground is already collapsing or when the water is already rising,” Mariano said. Residents in landslide-prone areas should also monitor changes in their surroundings and the condition of the soil, he said. “We should stay informed about our surroundings and know what is happening. If our area is landslide-prone, we should be aware if conditions are changing or if the soil has become too saturated,” Mariano said. “Based on that information, we should prepare and leave or evacuate immediately. This way, we can remain calm and know what to do to survive,” he added.

Monty Macalino remembers late Sleep Alley vocalist Aly Pagaduan. Mayonnaise's Monty Macalino paid tribute to late Sleep Alley vocalist Aly Pagaduan, recalling the alternative rock group’s potential while extending his condolences to her family and former bandmates. Macalino spoke about Pagaduan’s passing during a media conference for the upcoming Navotas Music Festival 2026. Note that Macalino had previously worked with Sleep Alley on one of the band’s releases. “So much talent in that group,” Macalino said, recalling how he saw considerable potential in the band during its early years. He remembered that Viva Records became interested in Sleep Alley while the group was recording its first album. Macalino supported the band’s move from Yellow Room to the major label, believing it would help further their career. “Sobrang may potential sila kaya sila kinuha ng Viva,” he said, describing the band’s sound at the time as “very raw” and “very college radio.” Sleep Alley confirmed Pagaduan’s death in a June 1 social media statement, describing her as more than a band member but “part of the heart and soul” of the group. The band highlighted her passion, creativity and friendship, saying she touched the lives of both her bandmates and listeners. The group did not disclose the cause of her death. Following her passing, Sleep Alley announced that it would close the chapter on the band as part of Pagaduan’s legacy. Macalino said he was shocked by the news, particularly because he knew Pagaduan was also involved with other bands. “Kaya nagulat na lang ako when she passed, when the news came that she passed away,” he said. He extended his condolences on behalf of Yellow Room to Pagaduan’s loved ones and the entire Sleep Alley community. “I’m truly sending our condolences from Yellow Room to the whole Sleep Alley family and to her family as well,” Macalino said. He also hoped Pagaduan’s music would continue to be heard, suggesting that other artists could perform Sleep Alley songs as a tribute to the late vocalist and the band’s work. “I hope that, kung pwede lang sana, kung may mga ibang tao na would pick up their songs and just to give tribute to such amazing talent na si Ally and the whole band, Sleep Alley,” he said. Macalino added that Sleep Alley bassist Jude still occasionally reaches out to him for advice, making Pagaduan’s passing an even more significant loss. Mayonnaise is set to perform at the inaugural Navotas Music Festival 2026 on Sept. 26 at the Navotas Convention Center. Presented by the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PCCI) – Navotas Chapter, the festival will also feature Cup of Joe, Maki, KAIA, and Room Session, alongside merchant booths, food hubs and lifestyle stalls. Tickets are available via Ticketmelon.

Laguna police locate man who had been missing for 5 years, reunite him with his family. CAMP VICENTE LIM, Laguna — The Police Regional Office 4A commended the Pangil Municipal Police Station for successfully locating and reuniting with the family an individual who had been reported missing for five years, on Aug. 9. The responding police led by Maj.Celso Jhune D. Talampas Pangil police, Cpl. Jerome Manzano, and Patrolwoman Rowena Sarambao, were recognized for their efforts. They spearheaded the arrangements and the safe transfer of the individual, known as alias John ,from the town of Cavinti to his family in Santa Rosa City. Beyond ensuring his safety, the local police also attended to the individual's well-being by providing proper clothing and food before formally reuniting him with his relatives. Police Brig. Gen Dominic L. Baccay, PRO4A director highlighted the compassionate service demonstrated by the Pangil Municipal Police Station, noting that it goes beyond the mere maintenance of peace and order. "Your police force is not solely focused on crime suppression and maintaining peace and order, but also on serving and addressing the needs of every citizen to the best of our ability—with love, readiness, and genuine concern for the community," said Baccay. With the return of every loved one, a family is given renewed hope—proof that the police force is always ready to respond, assist, and serve, he said.

Is Congress prioritizing VP Sara trial over calamity response? Deputy speakers say no. House Deputy Speakers La Union 1st district Rep. Paolo Ortega V and Iloilo 1st district Rep. Janette Garin defended Congress on Monday, Aug. 10 from criticisms that it was prioritizing Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial over response to problems caused by heavy rains and floods. Ortega, in an interview with reporters, said Congress was tending to both matters "equally". "Equally pinagtutunan po naman ang pansin yan. Yung executive side naman po nakatututok po sa problem, sa mas malalaking implementation at kailangan tutukan," he said. (Equal attention is given to that. The executive side focuses on the problem, on larger implementation, and what needs to be prioritized.) "Kami naman po on the legislative side, siyempre kung ano po maitutulong namin sa executive, sa implementation, tutulong po kami with legislative measures namin," noted Ortega. According to him, seeing through Duterte's impeachment trial is the lawmakers' constitutional mandate, and that it must be carried out along with their other functions, "As of now, siyempre may ongoing po tayo na impeachment. Bago naman po nagkaroon po ng calamity...na-anticipate naman po natin yan every year, yung rainy season. Pero kailangan po ma-[resolve] yung impeachment kasi this is an accountability measure, Constitution po yung sinusunod na," said the "Young Guns" bloc member. (As of now, of course we have ongoing impeachment. Even before the calamity...we anticipated the rainy season every year. But the impeachment must be resolved because this is an accountability measure, and it follows the Constitution.) The House of Representatives is acting as the prosecutor in Duterte’s impeachment trial, while the other legislative chamber, the Senate, serves as the court. For her part, Garin rejected claims that the House had prioritized the impeachment proceedings over the needs of communities affected by the inclement weather. She said Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III and Majority Leader Sandro Marcos have maintained daily coordination with the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and Department of Health (DOH). “For the past several days, hindi lang po ngayon, day-to-day ang coordination ni Speaker Bojie Dy at Majority Leader Sandro Marcos,” Garin said. (For the past several days, not just today, Speaker Bojie Dy and Majority Leader Sandro Marcos have been coordinating day‑to‑day.) She credited the DSWD for placing relief supplies closer to communities before the flooding instead of keeping all stocks in regional offices. “Ang DSWD, talagang maganda ang kanilang prepositioning. Wala lang sa regional offices ’yung kanilang mga food box, hygiene kits and family kits, pero ito ay nakalagay na sa maraming bayan-bayan.Patuloy ang pag-distribute ng food box, lalong-lalo na sa evacuation centers,” she added. (The DSWD has done well in its prepositioning. The food boxes, hygiene kits, and family kits are not only in regional offices but already placed in many towns. The distribution of food boxes continues, especially in evacuation centers.) 2027 budget process Garin said the House leadership was monitoring the response to identify immediate gaps and determine which programs may require additional funding in the upcoming 2027 budget process. “Nakatutok lang doon ang liderato ng Kongreso para makita namin, papasok ang budget season, kung ano ba ’yung kailangang i-augment at paano mas maging efficient,” she said. (Congress leadership is focused on this to see, as the budget season approaches, what needs to be augmented and how to make it more efficient.) The Marcos administration’s proposed P7.2-trillion budget for next year--as laid out in its 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP)--is set to begin submitted to the House tomorrow, Tuesday, Aug. 11. She identified agency quick response funds and the restoration of essential services—including clean water, power lines, roads and small bridges—as matters Congress could examine. “On the part of Congress, patuloy naming imo-monitor kung saan ang pangangailangan, ano ’yung immediate needs at paano ito matutugunan using our oversight powers,” Garin said. (On the part of Congress, we will continue to monitor where the needs are, what the immediate requirements are, and how these can be addressed using our oversight powers.) “Hindi puwedeng mahinto ’yung usapin ng accountability kasi it’s part of our constitutional duty,” she further said. (Accountability discussions cannot stop because it’s part of our constitutional duty.)

Philippines foreign investment plunges to lowest level in 11 years. Foreign direct investment (FDI) net inflows into the Philippines plunged to $210 million in May, the lowest monthly total in more than 11 years as global economic volatility and geopolitical tensions prompted foreign companies to delay capital commitments. According to the latest data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), released on Monday, Aug. 10, the May figure represents a 64.7 percent contraction from the level recorded in May 2025 and falls below the previous record low of $200.43 million seen in March 2015. The sharp monthly drop dragged total net inflows for the first five months of 2026 to $2.18 billion, a 33.4 percent decline from the $3.27 billion recorded in the same period last year. According to the BSP, the cumulative decline was “driven by lower foreign net investments in debt instruments and reinvestment of earnings, which more than offset the increase in net equity capital investments (other than reinvestment of earnings).” The central bank added that this trend “reflected lower intercompany borrowings from foreign direct investors and reduced earnings retained for reinvestment during the period.” Among its components, the primary driver of the May shrinkage was the sharp fall in net investments in debt instruments, which tumbled 92.1 percent to $35 million from $440 million a year earlier. As of end-May, debt instruments—which “consist mainly of intercompany borrowing or lending between foreign direct investors and their subsidiaries or affiliates in the Philippines”—totaled $1.25 billion, dropping by nearly half from the $2.48 billion recorded in 2025. This five-month performance follows a challenging 2025, during which annual net inflows plunged to $7.79 billion from $9.40 billion in 2024. The BSP forecasts inflows to clock in lower at $7 billion before rebounding to $8 billion in 2027. Despite the overall slump, the net equity component (excluding reinvestment of earnings) continued to show resilience. During the five-month period, this segment expanded by roughly 50 percent to reach $541 million, up from $364 million the previous year. Meanwhile, reinvestment of earnings during the five-month period fell by 9.7 percent to $383 million, down from $424 million a year ago. Equity capital placements during the first five months were sourced primarily from Japan, the United States, and Singapore. These investments were channeled largely into the manufacturing, financial and insurance, and real estate industries. FDI refers to cross-border investments where a non-resident investor owns at least 10 percent of the equity in a local enterprise; it consists of equity capital, reinvested earnings, and intercompany borrowings. These statistics track actual investment inflows reported in net terms (placements less withdrawals). Jonathan Ravelas, senior adviser at Reyes Tacandong & Co., said investors during the month “remained cautious amid heightened geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainties, and volatile financial markets, leading many firms to delay or scale back investment decisions.” Domestically, Ravelas noted that investors are watching for catch-up efforts the government is expected to deploy following muted performance since the second half of 2025. Clearer signals are expected on “policy execution, infrastructure rollout, power costs, and the overall ease of doing business.” Overall, Ravelas assessed the decline to be driven “more by investor caution than a loss of confidence in the Philippines,” adding that current trends signal selective investing rather than capital flight. “Looking ahead, FDI flows are likely to remain uneven in the near term as global uncertainty persists,” Ravelas said. “However, as interest rates continue to ease globally and supply chain diversification trends continue, the Philippines remains well-positioned to attract investments in manufacturing, logistics, digital infrastructure, renewable energy, and services.”

Asia Rose Simpson ready to shine at 73rd Miss World pageant. Miss World Philippines 2026 Asia Rose Simpson says she is "100% ready" to represent the Philippines at the 73rd Miss World pageant in Vietnam. The 18-year-old Filipina-American beauty queen shared her confidence during her send-off event in Quezon City on Aug. 6, where she talked about her preparations for the competition and its various fast-track events. For the Talent Fast Track, Simpson will perform "Succor," an original dance piece that explores mental health and the hope that remains accessible to everyone. She will also showcase her skills as an author and illustrator through "Mabuhay, Philippines," a children's book she wrote and illustrated for the Miss World Philippines Library. "I'm a children's book author and illustrator," Simpson said, adding that the book was inspired by people she has met and places she has visited in the Philippines. Simpson will also bring her SED (Sports, Exercise and Dance) initiative to the competition. The program promotes the physical and mental well-being of young people through sports, dance, workshops and mental health education. According to Simpson, the initiative has reached more than 10,000 young people in the Philippines, the United States and Vietnam. The send-off event also turned emotional as Simpson's family shared messages of support and encouragement before she leaves for the international competition. Simpson now heads to Vietnam hoping to make her mark at Miss World and bring the Philippines its second crown in the pageant. Megan Young won the country's first Miss World title in 2013.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. Click here to listen on Apple Podcasts or Spotify . For more, check out Sabine’s book “ The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response ”, and our Europe page.
